radiology_report:
ERASMUS MC | DEPARTMENT OF RADIOLOGY | 10 JAN 2025 | MULTIPARAMETRIC MRI PROSTATE

Clinical Indication:
Elevated PSA (8.7 ng/mL) and prior positive biopsy. Evaluation of rising PSA trajectory.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume measures 36.0 mL. T2-weighted imaging reveals a focal area of intermediate signal intensity in the right mid-gland peripheral zone, measuring approximately 12 mm in maximal dimension. Diffusion-weighted imaging demonstrates moderately restricted diffusion with corresponding low signal on the ADC map, consistent with a PI-RADS 3 category lesion. Dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging shows no early or focal enhancement. Seminal vesicles are unremarkable. No extraprostatic extension or suspicious pelvic lymphadenopathy is identified.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 3 lesion in the right mid-gland peripheral zone, measuring approximately 12 mm. Prostate volume 36.0 mL yielding a PSA density of 0.25 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.8735656.

previous_notes.author: Dr. E. Mulder (GP)
previous_notes.text: The patient was reviewed for a rising PSA trend, now at 5.7 ng/mL in July 2024 following an initial value of 3.2 ng/mL last winter. Repeat testing and free PSA fraction were obtained, showing a low percentage free PSA of 11%. Given the upward trajectory and prior histological confirmation of low-grade disease, he was subsequently referred to the urology outpatient clinic for further evaluation.
